meta.title: Isolated Solve-Then-Judge: A Simple Defense Against Candidate-Response Prompt Injection for Multimodal LLM Judges

units.text: We propose a two-pass architecture where the judge first generates its own answer using only trusted inputs, then uses this uncontaminated reference when evaluating candidates.
units.s2: Cost reports: none. Matched-budget comparisons: none.
units.found_note: S2.053 names “additional compute” with no number. S3.089 “comes at a cost” is accuracy (78.35% → 67.52%), not compute.
units.judge_line: Condition C has the same two passes, but nothing is compared with the single-pass baseline at the same number of calls.
units.final_reason: one extra model call per example, no cost number, no matched budget → cost 0 → FAIL

method.label: CONDITION B · THE DEFENSE · 2 MODEL CALLS

caps: The baseline judges in one call. The defense adds Pass 1 before the judgment: one more model call for every example.
Is that extra call measured anywhere? The result tables report accuracy and attack success only: no tokens, time or number of calls.
Two sentences say “compute” or “cost”, but neither measures what the defense costs to run.
Something is added and its cost is never reported → cost 0 → FAIL.
